brief:
Trump's incoming "Board of Peace" is preparing to seize Palestinian territory using administrative methods developed during the U.S. occupation of Iraq, Dawn reported. The approach relies on legal designations and bureaucratic mechanisms rather than direct military action, representing what Palestinians describe as a form of violence that persists beyond military campaigns.

The strategy reflects a pattern of administrative control that has historically outlasted armed conflict. Palestinian observers note this method of territorial appropriation operates through quiet legal mechanisms—designations, ledgers, and formal orders—that can prove more durable than conventional military occupation.
dek: Palestinians learn early that violence committed against them by Israel and its allies comes in many forms. Much of it is deadly, as the past three years of ongoing genocide in Gaza have shown. Another type of violence is administrative, arriving quietly, as a designation or line in a ledger, while outlasting the bombs that make the headlines.
title: Trump's peace board plans Palestinian land seizure modeled on Iraq occupation
